## The tasks

The exercise runs as five numbered tasks, and the report of the workspace, `index.qmd`, holds the steps of each.

### Task 1 – The setup check

Open the workspace folder in your IDE and run `source("R/check_setup.R")`, which prints OK when everything is in place and otherwise says what is missing.

### Task 2 – The data, the estimand and the graph

First, count what came back for each name in the `r format(nrow(housing), big.mark = ",")` emails of `housing_emails.csv` ([codebook](../../data/housing_emails_codebook.md)): the emails that bounced, the replies, and the replies that opened with the name of the sender.

Second, write the **estimand statement** behind the claim. It says which comparison is made (Hispanic names against which names), which emails are counted (the replies, or every delivered email), and which outcome is compared. The [specification menu](../../menu.qmd) gives the template.

Third, finish the **causal graph**. The graph shows why comparing greetings among the replies conditions on a consequence of the name: it compares only the emails that an official chose to answer, and the name may itself have changed that choice, which the [background page](../../background.qmd#sec-posttreatment) calls post-treatment conditioning. It also shows why counting every delivered email keeps the comparison as randomisation made it.

### Task 3 – The reproduction

Reproduce the analysis of one of the five analysts in the table above from the public file of the OAs, `housing_original.csv` ([codebook](../../data/housing_original_codebook.md)), in the tab of that analyst. Then find out why your number is what it is. A reproduction depends on the defaults and the codings of the software as well as on the data and the model.

### Task 4 – The menu

This task is **exploratory**: nothing in it is preregistered, and you may look, change your mind and try again. Try several specifications from the [specification menu](../../menu.qmd) with `try_spec()`, one decision at a time, and note which choices move the estimate and which barely touch it. Then choose the one that you would defend, and `submit_exploration()` sends it to the class chart on the [Class results](../../class-results.qmd) page, where it appears as an open circle.

### Task 5 – Preregistration

Choose **one** specification, one option for each decision, and complete the preregistration block **before you run it**. `run_spec()` fits the specification that you declared, and `report_result()` sends the declared result to the class chart, where it appears as a filled circle. Then find where your result sits on the curve of `r nrow(curve)` specifications.

Task 4 and Task 5 run the same code. An exploratory specification can have been chosen because of its result and a declared one cannot, and you submit both so that the two sets of class results can be compared.
